title: Uber Eats driver strike or stay-away over private platform fees
reason: The reported demands concern private Uber Eats fees and labor arrangements; no demand directed to the South African state or its policy is established. Evidence also does not establish a 50-person public gathering: offline-worker percentages and the 2,000-driver base are not crowd counts.
notes: Date conflicts: TimesLIVE planned a 22 January action, ITWeb and Citizen describe 22 January, while WSWS reports 21 January pickets. Citizen reports that the anticipated physical protest became a stay-away; ITWeb describes groups beside Johannesburg restaurants but gives no attendance count. A separate Gauteng strike on 18–19 December was reported suspended pending a company response, with no evidence of continuous physical action into January. This exclusion is about the private target and incomplete public-gathering evidence, not a claim that no work stoppage occurred.

title: Teachers’ union opposition to school reopening
reason: The opened SABC and TimesLIVE sources document policy objections and requests to education officials but no public gathering, march, picket or strike. A Citizen result was blocked and a regional Herald item remains search-only, so no qualifying event is established by the readable sources reviewed.
notes: This screening decision applies only to the sources reviewed; it does not establish that no teacher action occurred anywhere in South Africa during January.
